updates.statement: Step-indexed schedule reshuffles and trims are the finest schedule lever. On the head-lr tip, 2@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 (7.5 ep) beat 3@16 + 1@24 + 4@32 by +0.12 pp (pooled 0.7552 vs ~0.7540) for +0.9% time. That is about 1 SE, so it is weak. E070 (1.25@24, 7.25 ep) scored 0.7542 at 4.584 s, a single run with seed 2 at 0.7502. If its base lacks the Fable tail, adding the tail is the cheapest next gain. If the tail is present, the tail and the reshuffle do not stack. The trim slope of ~0.03-0.04 pp per 1% comes from single runs against lucky references and is unreliable. Fractional trims of the 32 px tail (~71% of time) have never been tested on a Muon base. The claim that 'the 32 px tail is binding' rests only on E025, whose base is ambiguous.
updates.reason: E064/E065 support H2.10.3, E070 is pending, and the review flags E070's provenance and the untested 32 px trims.

E064/E065 meet both preregistered bars: time 4.713/4.709 s (within 0.5% of E056's 4.718) and a two-run pool of 0.7552 (>=0.7540). The gain over the head-lr tip pool is only +0.12 pp at ~1 SE. E070, a further trim on this lineage, is pending its second scoring and a provenance check.

updates.statement: Freezing the whitening bias early leaves the stem with no trainable parameters, so autograd can skip group-1 conv1's input gradient and the stem backward in every later step. This is a FLOP lever that should transfer to the power-capped PCIe judge. Fable e1 and hiverge do it at ~0.2 epoch (about 7 steps at bs 1536 on CIFAR-100), not at 20% of steps, by switching requires_grad off and using separate compiled graphs keyed on whiten_bias_grad. E061 froze the bias via LR=0 at 20% of steps. That removed no compute, but it showed the freeze costs no accuracy (-0.08 pp, within noise), which is the precondition for this lever. The expected saving is modest (~0.5-1.5%), because group-1 conv1 has a narrow input (24 channels).
updates.reason: The search clarifies how the public recipes implement the freeze. The review notes E061 never tested the FLOP version, and its null accuracy result is a precondition rather than evidence against.

updates.statement: On the banked tip, set the whitening bias requires_grad=False after ~0.2 epoch (inside the 16 px phase), with separate static compiled graphs keyed by bias-grad, all warmed up in build on synthetic data. Change nothing else, and confirm in the compiled backward graph that the group-1 conv1 dgrad and the stem backward are gone. Prediction: time >=0.7% below the base's pooled time, and accuracy within 0.1 pp of the base (two scored runs plus an off-seed check). If the time drop is <0.3%, the dgrad is not being skipped or is negligible, and H2.15 is refuted as a time lever.
updates.reason: The freeze point now matches the public recipes, and the time prediction is resized for group-1 conv1's narrow input. E061's LR-only version leaves this untested.
E061 (whitening bias at LR 0 after 20% of steps) was null at -0.08 pp. The 64x-LR bias channel has no supporting effect, so the weak prior gets weaker.
Its pillars keep weakening: E051 and E059 are null, E061 is null, and E043 is confounded. Only E032 is large. It stays open as a weak prior.

updates.statement: Fused BN/GELU/elementwise Triton kernels take 29-31% of GPU time at 24/32 px (E067), but the cost is spread over ~211 kernels per step; the top kernel takes ~0.43 ms/step. Inductor tuning flags are near-optimal and blow the build budget (E066). Torch 2.4 has no fused normalization-backward codegen (that arrived ~2.11), so BN backward likely reads dy and x in separate reduction and dX passes. The only lever left is a hand-written Triton fused BN(+GELU) backward for the dominant 32 px layers. It is math-equivalent and saves energy-proportional bytes, but it costs high effort and has a bounded gain. A bias-only BN (frozen weight), as in Fable/hiverge, saves essentially no backward compute, because dX needs both per-channel reductions anyway.
updates.reason: E067 supports the elementwise share. E066 refuted the flag route. The search on Inductor's normalization backward explains the null result and leaves only a hand-written kernel.
E067 shows Triton elementwise/reduction kernels at 29% (32 px) and 31% (24 px) of GPU time, which clears the >=25% bar. The pass count per activation was not reported, so the support is partial.

E066 ran the flag route (coordinate_descent_tuning + max_autotune_pointwise): -0.1% time and a ~554 s build, far short of the >=2% predicted. The hand-written Triton route is split out as a separate low-prior child.
E067 was supposed to capture per-layer group-2 conv times, but none were reported. The test is still open: pull the numbers from that profile before any width run.

updates.statement:
Accuracy noise sets the usable margin, and near-gate decisions select for luck. Per-run sd of the 3-seed mean is ~0.15 pp, the same size as the zero-cost effects being chased (0.1-0.2 pp). Pooling rule, fixed:
- Every same-math run counts, whatever its sign; math-neutral variants count (reduction order, static shapes, pool swap, prepare fusion), so E066 (0.7570) belongs in the head-lr family.
- Bit-identical reruns (E044/E045, E062/E067) count once.
- A run whose source hash is not logged is not pooled until its provenance is verified.
Under this rule the head-lr family (E062, E063, E066) is ~0.7550, and every 'supports' verdict since E057 is ~1-2 SE. Time noise between same-code runs is ~0.5-0.8% (E057/E058, E068/E069), not 0.3%. Compare times against pooled family times. The official gate is a 40-seed mean, and accuracy-changing levers since E048 have had no off-seed check. Untimed seeds 3-10 should be the default A/B instrument for zero-cost accuracy levers.
updates.reason: The review shows uneven pool membership (E066 excluded, E067 double-counted), wider-than-assumed time noise, and no off-seed checks since E048.

E067 was bit-identical per seed to E062, as E045 was to E044, while other same-code reruns diverged by 0.1-0.6 pp per seed. That fits the bimodal picture: some processes reproduce training exactly, others diverge.

Two bit-identical rerun pairs next to divergent reruns fit a discrete mixture over per-process cuDNN pick sets with near-tied benchmarks. Per-seed spread also varies widely between runs (E063 0.7543-0.7548 vs E070 0.7502-0.7571). The kernel-name logging requested in E067 was not reported, so this stays weak support.

updates.statement: Provenance check, untimed. Diffing e6c8e93 (E048) and 4fd9ea5 (E052) against 2fda094 (E046) shows only instrumentation changes. 5a77f89 (E053) and 6262ecd (E056) differ only by the static-shape config and the pool. Diffing e945ed5 (E070) against a1aef09 (E064) and 766d5bf (E068) shows whether E070 contains the Fable tail. On one fixed batch, max(dim).values and AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) gradients match except at fp16 ties. Any failure means the affected runs leave the pooled baselines.
updates.reason: The review's top critique: E070's description puts it on pre-tail E064 code while the notebook calls it the tail tip. That diff is folded into this provenance check.

new.statement: The E070 code (e945ed5) lacks the Fable tail, which the diff against 766d5bf would show. Adding the tail unchanged to E070's 2@16 + 1.25@24 + 4@32 schedule then gives a two-run pooled accuracy >=0.7560 at time within ±0.8% of E070's 4.584 s. If the diff shows the tail is already present, the tail and the 24 px reshuffle do not stack, and H6.5.2 or H2.10.3 (at least one) is a noise draw.

On the verified tail tip, cut the 32 px tail by 0.25 epoch (… + 3.75@32, step-indexed switch, LR/EMA/lookahead/renorm rescaled to the step count). Prediction: time drops ~4-5% (~0.2 s) and accuracy falls by <=0.15 pp (two scored runs plus an off-seed seeds 3-10 check), i.e. <=0.035 pp per 1%, comparable to 24 px trims. If the loss is >=0.3 pp, the 32 px tail is binding and trims should come from the 24 px bridge.

On the verified tail tip, run two single-change ablations: (a) remove only the final EMA (eval on the net weights, floor-hold and lookahead stop kept) and (b) remove only the floor-hold (decay ends at the last step, final EMA kept). Each gets one scored run plus an off-seed seeds 3-10 check. Prediction: one component accounts for >=2/3 of the tail's gain over the pre-tail family, so ablating it costs >=0.1 pp, while ablating the other costs <=0.05 pp. Whichever carries the gain becomes the next tuning axis (EMA length/decay vs floor level).

On the verified tip, set the head's Muon lr to 0.4x the filter lr (instead of 0.5x; a separate 0-d tensor, nothing recompiles), close to the spectral-condition scale sqrt(100/576) ≈ 0.42. Prediction: accuracy >= the 0.5x arm +0.05 pp, measured as a two-run pool plus off-seed seeds 3-10, at equal time. If 0.4x is >=0.1 pp worse, the head optimum is at or above 0.5x and head lr is closed.

Label smoothing at 0.3 penalizes the ground-truth logit. MaxSup (CE + α(z_max − mean_k z_k)) penalizes the top-1 logit instead, which keeps the regularization while removing LS's error-amplification on misclassified examples. On CIFAR-100 ResNets it beat LS by 0.27-0.77 pp, albeit on 200-epoch schedules. It is zero-cost and orthogonal to the closed LS-value knob (E009, E037).

On the verified tip, replace LS 0.3 with plain CE + 0.3·(max_k z_k − mean_k z_k) (one fused op on [B,100] logits; smoke-test 10 steps for finite loss under compile). Prediction: an off-seed seeds 3-10 mean and a two-run scored pool both >= the tip's +0.15 pp at time within ±0.5%. A result within ±0.1 pp closes it.

Regularization should scale with image size (EfficientNetV2 adaptive regularization: +0.7-0.8 pp over plain progressive resizing). The low-res 16/24 px phases are under-fit (E008: more augmentation hurt), so a uniform LS 0.3 over-regularizes them, while the 32 px tail benefits from it. A uniform LS change was null (E037), so only the phase-dependent variant is untested.

On the verified tip, use LS 0.15 during the 16/24 px phases and 0.3 in the 32 px tail (a 0-d tensor or per-phase loss constant; no recompile beyond the existing per-resolution graphs). Prediction: an off-seed seeds 3-10 mean and a two-run scored pool >= the tip's +0.15 pp at equal time. A result within ±0.1 pp closes it.

Untimed margin check. The current tip (E070, or E070 plus the tail once provenance is settled), run through the benchmark's trial code on seeds 3-10, gives a mean >=0.7530 that lies within 0.15 pp of its seeds 0-2 pool. If the mean is <0.7520, the margin spent since E048 is gone, and accuracy must be added before any further cut.

Per-trial time logs over >=4 same-code runs show trial 1 slower than trials 2-3 by >=0.5% on average (E069: trial 1 4.757 vs mean 4.708). That would mean some lazy init still leaks into the first timed trial (e.g. allocator growth, a cuBLAS workspace or cuDNN plan for a shape not warmed in build). Warming those paths in build would then cut mean time by >=0.3% at identical math. If trial 1 is not systematically slower, the E069 outlier is noise.

A hand-written Triton kernel for the 32 px group-2/3 layers fuses the per-channel reductions (sum dy, sum dy·xhat) with the dX/GELU-backward pass, reading dy and x once instead of twice. It is warmed up in build and math-equivalent up to fp16 rounding. Prediction: time drops >=1.5% with accuracy within noise (two-run pool within 0.1 pp of base). Write the bytes-moved estimate down before scoring. Low priority: high effort, and the elementwise share is spread over many fusions.

structured_output.summary:
Tree synced with the verdicts from E057 to E070 and re-baselined per the review.

- **Statements rewritten:** the H2 and H6 Lvl1 statements now describe the current state: tip family ~4.67 s, provisional E070 at 4.584 s with its base unclear, and the Fable tail worth ~+0.12 pp against a fixed pooling baseline rather than +0.25.
- **Pooling rule (H4):** all same-math runs count regardless of sign, so E066 is in. Bit-identical reruns count once, and runs without a logged source hash wait for provenance. Time noise is now ~0.5-0.8%, and untimed off-seed checks become the A/B instrument.
- **Status changes:**
  - Refuted: H6.5.1 (floor 0.05), H6.4.2 (doubled warmup), H2.16.2 (Inductor flags).
  - Retired: H6.4.
  - Inconclusive: H7.3.2 (missed its bar by rounding).
  - Supported with lowered magnitude: H6.5.2 (tail) and H2.10.3 (2@16 + 1.5@24 reshuffle).
  - Supported: H2.16.1 (elementwise kernels ~30% of GPU time).
- **H2.15 rewritten:** the whitening-bias freeze uses requires_grad=False at ~0.2 epoch. E061 only tested the LR route, so it showed the accuracy cost is nil but not the time saving.
- **New hypotheses:**
  - Provenance: E070's diff folded into H4.2.4, then E070 plus the tail.
  - Schedule: a fractional trim of the 32 px tail (never tested).
  - Tail: ablation of its components.
  - Head: Muon lr 0.4x (spectral scale sqrt(100/576)).
  - Loss: MaxSup and phase-dependent label smoothing, both search-sourced.
  - Margin: an off-seed seeds 3-10 check on the current tip.
  - Timing: a trial-1 lazy-init leak.
  - Kernels: a hand-written Triton fused BN backward (low priority).
- **Open Lvl1:** H2, H4, H6 and H8.
